v2 VOLTAGE DROP — SOURCE-GATED CIRCUIT CHECK

Voltage-drop calculations use circuit current, one-way route length, power factor, and design R/X impedance. Manufacturer/database R/X values may be used for screening only when their temperature/basis is not the actual operating AC impedance. Manual design-impedance overrides therefore take precedence. When the installed/current conductor exceeds the entered project VD limit, the automatic upsize engine identifies the smallest larger source-verified compatible cable-database variant that meets the limit. This recommendation does not overwrite the NEC ampacity release or silently replace the user's selected cable.

cells.value: Engineering basis: Southwire's installation guide uses voltage drop based on cable resistance/reactance and load power factor, with separate two-wire/single-phase and three-phase relationships. This module deliberately treats database R/X as screening-only unless the values are confirmed for the actual operating temperature and installation. The entered voltage-drop limit is a project design criterion; it is not presented here as a universal mandatory NEC limit.

v2 CABLE SHORT-CIRCUIT THERMAL WITHSTAND — ADIABATIC CHECK

Checks I²t thermal withstand using I²t ≤ k²S². Exact/verified cable insulation is used when available; otherwise a verified planning-key insulation class may support screening. When the project fault input is PEAK kA, the module uses Peak/√2 as a conservative upper bound for RMS symmetrical current. Final k remains review-gated whenever the supported initial-temperature basis is not established.

Source boundary: ABB's electrical-installation handbook gives the adiabatic cable relation and representative k values for Cu/Al with PVC, EPR/XLPE and rubber insulation. Automatic k is used only when the conductor temperature rating does not exceed the source table's stated initial-temperature basis. Otherwise the workbook requires a source-backed manual k. If the project input is peak current only, this thermal module does not reverse-convert it to RMS; enter the RMS symmetrical fault value from the short-circuit study.
Thermal withstand >= fault/set using a manually confirmed k
Missing RMS fault, duration or conductor data
Automatic k / parallel-current assumption requires engineering confirmation
FAIL > INPUT REQUIRED > REVIEW REQUIRED > PASS
v2 CABLE PULL / INSTALLATION PLAN — CABLE TRAY & CONTROLLED BENDS

Installation-planning module based on Southwire cable-installation equations. It distinguishes open-tray straight/vertical sections from frictional or conduit-type bends. Maximum pulling tension and any project-specific sidewall-pressure limit remain cable/manufacturer/project inputs; they are not invented by the calculator.

cells.value: Engineering boundary: Southwire distinguishes cable tray pulls from conduit pulls. With well-maintained rotating sheaves at tray bends, the bend does not have the same frictional multiplication as a fixed conduit bend; however, the force required to bend heavier cable is still real and is not invented here. Select “Frictional / Controlled Bend” only when conduit-type bend equations are appropriate. Sidewall pressure is calculated only for that segment type and only for the source-supported one/common-jacket, 3-conductor cradled, or triangular arrangements.
